newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to clear Lyonnaise/Suez merger.
newsitem.headline: EU to clear Lyonnaise/Suez merger.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Tuesday that the Commission would clear in the next few days the merger between Lyonnaise des Eaux and Compagnie de Suez creating a global utilities heavyweight.

Van Miert, who was talking to reporters, said approval was made possible after the companies agreed to address Commission concerns that the deal would give the two partners too strong a hold in the Belgian market for waste management.

"Both companies are active in this market. Once the problem was identified they had a choice between offering fully fledged remedies or we would have gone into a second phase (detailed probe)," Van Miert said as he arrived for a conference organised by the Wall Street Journal Europe.

French utility giant Lyonnaise des Eaux offered to have its subsidiary Sita sell off its 49-percent stake in waste management firm PAGE, Belgian steel maker Cockerill Sambre, which indirectly owns the remaining shares in PAGE, said late on Monday.

The proposed merger ends the independence of Suez, set up in the 19th century to build the Suez Canal, a glory of French engineering. Lyonnaise is twice the size of Suez in terms of shareholder funds and one third bigger in share capitalisation.
The new group, to be called Suez Lyonnaise, will have annual sales of more than 200 billion francs ($34.3 billion) and a market capitalisation of 75 billion francs.

The Commission has until Thursday to make an official announcement on the merger which was submitted for clearance under EU rules banning creation or strengthening of dominant positions at the end of April.
Under the EU's merger rules the Commission can block or impose strict conditions on agreements found to harm fair competition.
Van Miert said the two partners had made the concessions in the field of waste management at the end of last week.
The new group will focus on four core business -- energy, water distribution, waste management and communications. ($ = 5.825 French Francs)
